chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly substrate teaching with minimal editorial overlay. The oldest layer dominates: a systematic cosmological teaching about the Ambassador's image display, the rulers' unauthorized fashioning of Adam and Eve as an imperfect copy, and a three-fold enumeration of figures fashioned outside intercourse (sea giant, sea monster/Adamant, vegetation). A correspondential parable (the noble woman) is embedded as a teaching device — both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system. The only clearly non-substrate material is the dialogue frame attribution in ¶2, the pedagogical address formulas in ¶1/3/9, and the transitional marker in ¶8. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortation layers are detectable. The substrate vocabulary actually increases in the second half, consistent with the chapter-level shift data (+0.44). The term 'crucified in the totality' in ¶7 is distinctively Manichaean but describes cosmic process rather than contemporary application.

paragraphs.core_text: There are some amo]ng us telling us that we [know (?) ... ] that the (Ambassador) consents about [tha]t f[igure] of flesh; he who shall be fashi[oned ... ] at another time. And next, he says: [The Ambassa]dor displayed his image in the un[iverse]. The rulers and the powers of the universe saw h[is image], and they formed their shapes after his likeness, who are Adam and Eve. Behold, you see that god con[sen]ts to its happening; because of this, he has displayed his image to the rulers; and they constructed [ ... ... ] If he was not consenting to humankind, he would not have uncovered his image, nor they fashioned mankind after his likeness!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: '[Once more his] disciples questioned the glorious one. They say to [him:' — standard disciple-question frame wrapping a substantive cosmological argument.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The question is substantive — it presents the cosmological argument that the Ambassador's image display implies divine consent to the human form. The cosmological content (Ambassador displayed image → rulers formed shapes → Adam and Eve) defines the teaching topic. 'There are some among us' references the community but is part of the question's substance in the Persian dialogue tradition.

paragraphs.core_text: Regarding the Ambassador, the occasion when he came displaying his image, he [d]id not come so th[a]t he might reveal his image to the ru[l]ers in the universe. Rather, he came and displayed to the universe be[cause of h]is soul and his son, who is [ ... ] every [ ... ], that he might enable him to live [ ... ] and make for him a release; and to free (the soul) from every bond and all the fetters, in which it is entangled and bound.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: '⟨p.133⟩ Then speaks the glorious one to his disciples:' — formulaic speaker introduction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The teaching content is pure substrate: the Ambassador's purpose was to free the soul from bonds and fetters, not to reveal his image to rulers. 'Soul-body binding formula' (bonds, fetters, entangled, bound) is a classic substrate marker. The negation-correction structure ('did not come so that... Rather...') is a teaching device clarifying cosmic process.

paragraphs.core_text: The rulers and the authorities, in that they had no form in [ ... ] him, they lusted for his image. They reflected upon themselves, that [they] had no [one] like him in their creation. They sealed hi[s im]a[g]e in their heart, within their soul. Afterward[s, they] built it according to his likeness; they formed Adam and [Ev]e. They sealed the image of the exalted one in their [soul]. So, they [co]pied with an imitation; but they have not [copied i]n truth! Rather, just as [ ... ... ] it is made as these, for [i]t came [ ... ] but it is not l[ik]e him in truth. [Again, so too] is this figure of ma[nkind. They copi]ed it against the image of the exalted one [ ... ]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed pedagogical address: 'Still, you, look and see!' — direct audience address formula that frames the following cosmological content.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core teaching about the mechanism of unauthorized fashioning: rulers lusted → sealed image in their soul → built according to likeness → copied with imitation, not in truth. The distinction between 'imitation' and 'truth' is a fundamental substrate category — the copy is not the original. The process described (seal → build → form) is systematic cosmological process.

paragraphs.core_text: Similarly the [t]ree, for while it is like the [ ... it is] not [copi]ed in truth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief substrate continuation extending the imitation/truth distinction to the tree. The tree analogy maps within the cosmic system — vegetation as another domain of imperfect copying. Despite heavy lacunae, the substrate logic is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: This matt[er is comparable to] this: As a great, fre[e] woman [ ... ] within her [ ... ... ] rich in wealth [ ... ] po[ss]essions; she is also beautiful in her beauty, and is virtuous in her modesty. She walks in a free and reputable position. The fame of her beauty has spread in every c[i]ty. She sur[passes ... ] Behold h[er] chamber [ ... ] one who is mad, because [of] the nobles and the great ones. Al[so], they lust for her beautiful face. They did not [ ... ] her, because she is hidden in her palace [ ... ] within in a [ ... ] meet that woman [ ... ] his so[n]; or rather the head [ ... t]hat garment. This free woman shall [ ... ] leave the cha[mber] behind her and come to the street [ ... ] her head [ ... ] and she reveals her [face and her beauty ... ] because of her beloved broth[er]. This wom[an], on whom no man ever looked, nor did they ever see her fa[ce], as she neither desires nor rejoices [ ... ... ] leave her chamber behind her, and come in the midst of mankind [ ... ] and everyone view her. The hones[t] men and the nobles, even the servants too, and the [ ... ] look at her.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The parable is a teaching simile: the noble woman hidden in her palace who reveals herself to save her brother corresponds to the Ambassador revealing his image to rescue the entrapped soul. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system — this is correspondence being used as a teaching method, not pointing to contemporary institutions. The 'comparable to' formula is a standard teaching introduction in the Persian pedagogical tradition. Significant lacunae but the correspondential structure is intact.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.135⟩ In accord with this simile: Again, [this] too [is] how [ ... ] the Ambassador becomes [ ... ... ] as this free woman [ ... not] according to wantonness, in pride, nor [ ... she co]nsented to the outer world, she [ ... ... ], she revealed her face and her [beau]ty [ ... ] but only due to the constraint of grief [about] her [bel]ov[ed one].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the correspondential mapping: the Ambassador = the free woman. The revelation was not from wantonness but from grief over the beloved one (the entrapped soul/son). Both sides of the mapping stay in the cosmic system. 'In accord with this simile' is a teaching structural marker. Heavy lacunae but the teaching logic is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this too is the way of the Third Ambassador, when he came and display[ed his] image with a show towards all the powers. [He did] not [co]me so that all the rulers and the author[it]ies would sculpt a form [after h]is likeness. R[ather], he came because of his son being crucified in the totality; [fo]r he would release him, free him, and rescue him from oppres-sion. Yet, when the rulers looked o[n] him, [th]ey lusted for his image. They fashioned after his [like]ness Adam and Eve, without the consent of the gre[at]ness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Restates the substrate teaching with specificity: the Third Ambassador's purpose was release/rescue, not consent to fashioning. 'Crucified in the totality' is distinctively Manichaean christological language (Jesus patibilis concept), but here it describes a cosmic state — the son/soul distributed and entrapped in matter — not a contemporary application. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. 'Without the consent of the greatness' explicitly answers the question posed in ¶1.

Pure dialogue frame transitional marker. First-person address ('I have enlightened you'), reference to the question asked, instruction to memorize. No cosmological content whatsoever. Functions as an editorial seam between the first teaching section (Ambassador/Adam) and the second (stamp of the image on powers).

paragraphs.core_text: For, [a]s with Adam and Eve, whom the rulers fashioned and [se]aled after the image of the exalted one, so too this [i]s how a manifold divinity and many powers and angels [ ... received] the stamp of that image, which was displayed to them. For, in the majesty of the l[ig]ht and (the image's) love, they glowed with their desire and they were undone. Th[ey] were eager for their lust; like a m[an who looks] to the majesty of a lusted after face, and [ ... ] and he is eager for the {} of the desire.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed pedagogical frame: '[Understa]nd also this other (matter) that I will teach you.' — first-person teaching introduction formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extends the substrate teaching: not only Adam and Eve but also many powers and angels received the stamp of the displayed image. The teaching maps cosmic process: image display → desire → stamp reception. The simile ('like a man who looks to the majesty of a lusted after face') is a teaching device within the substrate, mapping human experience back to cosmic process.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.136⟩ This is [als]o the case with those powers, when they looked on that majestic and beautiful [imag]e, they () [ ... ] a first image. They received the stamp of th[at image], which was displayed to them. They copied [ ... wh]ich th[ey co]pied out in a likeness, it being made [ ... ... ] the ones that they had put forth, which had received a [stamp of this im]age; but inward even to the rocks [ ... ... ] which occur from place to place. The {} of that image, which was displayed in the universe [ ... ] they received a stamp, it being revealed there, and an impress.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues substrate teaching about the stamp of the image permeating the cosmos — from powers down to rocks. This is a systematic degree-mapping: the image's stamp extends through levels of being (powers → their productions → rocks). Both sides stay within the cosmic system. The term 'impress' alongside 'stamp' suggests a technical vocabulary of image-transmission in the substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this new birth that they begot in a new [ ... ] in the world, is Adam and Eve. [There is not a] form in their world since the beginning like it; because that [im]age [occ]urs not in the worlds b[el]ow.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate teaching identifying Adam and Eve as unprecedented — a 'new birth' with no prior form in the lower worlds. The image occurs not in the worlds below, establishing that the human form derives from above, not from the dark realms. Maps cosmic geography (worlds below) to the origin of form.

paragraphs.core_text: Not all the figures that have been fashioned were fashioned by birth from displayed intercourse. Rather, there are other figures fashioned [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces the three-fold enumeration of figures fashioned outside intercourse. This is a structural transition within the substrate — it sets up the systematic list that follows. The distinction between intercourse-fashioned and otherwise-fashioned figures is a cosmological category.

paragraphs.core_text: One of them is the sea [gi]ant, the 'sweeping' from the sphere, which the [Father] of Life discharged into the sea. Its own fire and thought fashioned it [in] a figure.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. The sea giant was fashioned by its own fire and thought — an internal fashioning process, not sexual generation. 'Sweeping from the sphere' and 'Father of Life discharged into the sea' are cosmic process descriptions. The enumeration marker 'One of them is' is integral to the teaching structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The second figure is the one [that] fell to the earth. It made the sea its womb. Its own l[us]t became its sculptor. It alone fashioned it to a nature, which is the root of death. Yet, when it came up from the sea, it [ ... ] that it might destroy the works [ ... ] of Life. They immediately sent against it the Adamant of Light, the great 'instruction of vigour'. He humbled it in the districts of the north. He has trampled underfoot and set h[im]self upon it, until the end of the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. Rich substrate content: the figure's own lust as sculptor, the sea as womb, 'root of death' as cosmic category. The Adamant of Light subduing it 'in the districts of the north' is cosmic geography. 'Until the end of the world' is cosmological time-frame, not editorial eschatology. The substrate vocabulary score (4.12) is the highest in the chapter, confirming the cosmological density.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.137⟩ [The] third figure is the nature that fell on wh[at] is dr[y. It] fashioned the tree and set itself there. [ ... the] new figure that was fashioned [ ... d]isplays.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit, heavily lacunose. The nature fell on dry land and fashioned the tree. This completes the three-fold pattern: sea giant (sea), sea monster (sea→earth), vegetation (dry land). The spatial mapping (sea/earth/dry) is systematic cosmic geography. Connects back to the tree mentioned briefly in ¶4.

paragraphs.core_text: So, in accord with the essence they [ ... the dark]ness; but yet th[ey] did not come with the King of Dark[ness to the wo]rld. Rather, their fashioning [came] about [ ... ] they are composite and have been displayed in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding substrate summary for the three-fold enumeration. These figures are from Darkness in essence but did not arrive with the King of Darkness — they are 'composite,' fashioned during the cosmic history from the mixture. This is a fundamental cosmological category: composite beings that belong neither purely to light nor to darkness. The teaching completes the chapter's argument: the human form and these other figures are products of the cosmic process, not of original divine or dark design.
